newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu names new commander of Zaire land forces.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu names new commander of Zaire land forces.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, currently at his villa in the South of France, has shaken up the army high command, naming a new commander of land forces, state radio reported on Saturday.

General Mosala Modjandongo, commander of the Lower Zaire region, had been promoted to the job, replacing General Mulumba Ambote, it said, quoting a presidential decree signed by Mobutu on February 17, before his departure for France.
The shake-up follows advances by rebels from the east on several fronts, blunting an army counter-offensive launched from Zaire's third city of Kisangani on January 20.

Defence officials contacted by Reuters on Saturday were unable to elaborate on the reasons for the latest change in the high command, whose forces are struggling against mainly Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms last October.
Mobutu, who had prostate surgery last August in Europe, returned to Zaire after four months absence and reshuffled the army high command in December.

He appointed General Mahele Lieko Bokungo chief of staff of the armed forces with sweeping powers. Mahele is one of the rare senior ranking generals in Zaire who has earned his reputation on the battlefield and not through close family or ethnic ties to Mobutu.
